name: Immune Dysregulation-Inflammatory Bowel Disease-Arthritis-Recurrent Infections Syndrome
aliases: Immune Dysregulation Syndrome with IBD and Arthritis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Immune Dysregulation-IBD-Arthritis-Recurrent Infections Syndrome

criteria.description: Evidence of immune dysregulation including abnormal lymphocyte subsets or cytokine profiles
Clinical, endoscopic, or histopathological confirmation of inflammatory bowel disease
Clinical or radiological evidence of arthritis affecting peripheral or axial joints
History of recurrent bacterial, viral, or fungal infections requiring medical intervention
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with immune regulation
Exclusion of other known primary immunodeficiencies or autoimmune syndromes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all four major criteria: immune dysregulation, inflammatory bowel disease, arthritis, and recurrent infections
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing and immunological profiling support diagnosis but are not mandatory.

searchTerms: chronic immune system overactivity with lymph node swelling
excessive lymphocyte growth from immune problems

pathognomonic.symptomName: Early-onset inflammatory bowel disease with granulomatous inflammation
searchTerms: early childhood inflammatory bowel disease with granulomas
young onset gut inflammation with granuloma

pathognomonic.symptomName: Recurrent severe bacterial infections including pneumonia and otitis media
searchTerms: frequent severe bacterial infections like pneumonia

common.symptomName: Symmetric polyarthritis involving small and large joints
searchTerms: joint swelling and pain in many joints symmetrically
arthritis affecting small and large joints
chronic diarrhea accompanied by abdominal cramps

common.symptomName: Failure to thrive or growth retardation
Cutaneous manifestations such as erythematous rash or eczema

searchTerms: temporary low neutrophil or lymphocyte counts

laboratory: Abnormal lymphocyte subset analysis (e.g., decreased regulatory T cells)
imaging: Joint X-rays showing synovitis or erosions
Abdominal MRI or CT showing bowel wall thickening and inflammation
Chest imaging demonstrating recurrent pneumonia or bronchiectasis
other: Endoscopic biopsy showing granulomatous inflammation in the gastrointestinal tract

distinguishingFeatures: Predominantly antibody deficiency without characteristic arthritis or IBD
Later onset and less frequent granulomatous bowel inflammation
Arthritis and IBD without recurrent severe infections or immune dysregulation laboratory abnormalities
Lack of systemic immune dysregulation features
Presence of endocrine autoimmune disorders and chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis

redFlags: Early-onset inflammatory bowel disease refractory to standard therapies
Failure to thrive or growth delay in pediatric patients
references: Orphanet: Immune Dysregulation-Inflammatory Bowel Disease-Arthritis-Recurrent Infections Syndrome, ORPHA:238569
